main_issue: How Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling food (fish curry) without the smell disrupting A's work calls, B's room and C's laundry.

A-B.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling cooking (T1); B said it gets into her room (T2) and later accepted D's window-and-hood plan (T23). They never address each other directly.

A-C.evidence: Both complained about the smell (T1, T3). A wanted cooking after 7pm on weekdays or Saturday (T5), and C agreed to Tue/Thu/weekend (T21), which is compatible with A's request. They never address each other.

A-D.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling food (T1). D apologised and offered a compromise (T4). A proposed after 7pm or Saturday (T5), D accepted (T6), and the final plan keeps after 7pm and the weekend (T18, T27).

B-C.evidence: Both said the timing doesn't fix the smell (T8, T9). C doubted that the hood would be enough (T15), while B accepted the hood plan (T23). Neither addresses the other.

B-D.evidence: B said changing the time doesn't help (T8) and suggested the window and hood (T14). D offered to open the window and use the hood every time (T22) and B accepted (T23); D called it settled (T27).

C-D.evidence: C said the time doesn't help (T9) and asked for weekends only (T11). D questioned it (T12, T16), C narrowed it to Mon/Wed/Fri laundry (T17), D offered Tue/Thu/weekend (T18), and C accepted (T21).
